parsed.basis: Barisal Division in south-central Bangladesh is a largely rural, riverine, overwhelmingly Muslim region with limited foreign tourism and few large-city support or legal-aid networks compared with Dhaka. No Barisal-specific law, protective programme, or tourism exception distinguishes it from the national regime. Bangladesh retains Penal Code Section 377 criminalising consensual same-sex intercourse with imprisonment up to life, police documented using it and suspicious-behaviour provisions to harass effeminate and visibly gender-nonconforming people, with extortion, arbitrary arrest, and retaliatory violence in 2025. Third-gender recognition since 2013 applies mainly to hijra identity without general protection against discrimination or violence. If outed, a visitor would face social hostility, police harassment or extortion, possible detention, and very limited effective recourse locally.
